title: People say my browser puzzle game "looks cool", then play and leave after just a few minutes. What am I missing?
author: TommyGameDev
selftext:
Hey everyone!

For the last few months I’ve been working on a puzzle game, [lasergrid.app](https://lasergrid.app/?from=rd-aigamedev), and I struggle to get players to stay for longer than 5 minutes. I’ve gotten comments on reddit like "looks cool" and "loved it", but players don’t stick or return to the game.

In the game you guide lasers by bouncing them off mirrors that you turn, so the laser reaches every crystal. There’s also an added element of catching all the stars along the way by correctly utilizing all the pieces on the board (which is optional)

Since Saturday, a few dozen new people tried it. More than half finished level 1, about half got to level 3, but only very few made it past the intro levels. And the weird part is that for almost half of them, the last thing they did before they left, was win their level.

If you give it a try, I'd really like to know where you would have stopped, and why.

I’m not sure if the problem is that it's:

* boring, too difficult / too easy, or just not appealing.
* Needs more help and hints for casual players?
* Feel like slop or the sound is off-putting?
* Or I just didn't find the right audience yet?

Hope you can help me! Any feedback is much appreciated

comments.author: TommyGameDev
comments.body:
Right, I agree. This game is also not meant for very long sessions, and for this an app game would be a lot better than a browser game.   
I guess it also needs a bit more satisfaction to get that shower dopamine hit that people want, I’m just not sure what needs to change. 

Thank you, I appreciate the feedback!

replies.author: kytheon
replies.body:
I played for a few levels and checked some harder levels too. It seems alright. Not spectacular but functional. I've played games like this decades ago. 

One game design issue I found: when I finish a level it says "⭐️, you missed two stars."

Then I get to completely replay the level from the start. Let me continue from the solved state so I can change it a bit and get the other stars. I don't want to redo the level.

comments.author: Sumchi
comments.body: I felt like its just another puzzle game with the same mechanics you see in every other puzzle game. I couldn't stay interested past level 6

comments.author: Prestigious_Edge_472
comments.body:
I played 3 levels, I have the sound off so no comment there.   
I don't think there is anything wrong with it personally, it's just a puzzle game, it's interesting for 2 seconds but then that's it.  
I don't think implementation can change the level of interest for this type of game to be honest, there is a reason why you see those as mini-games in other games that people generally aren't too fond off to begin with.  
My 2 cents

comments.author: TommyGameDev
comments.body:
Thank you for the feedback, I appreciate it!

Yes, I get that it might look a bit one-shotted, and I will say that most of the work has gone into making the procedural level generator, so it actually spits out challenging levels (at least later in the game).

I feel like the game becomes much more fun when the later mechanics are introduced, especially the expert and master chapters with the linked grids mechanic, which I haven’t seen before. But I’m also biased since I made the game, I’ll admit that.

I did also put a lot of work into the “looks” packages to make it more fun, but most people don’t even try them out.

comments.author: shaymagen
comments.body: usually it's the first 30 seconds. if people have to read or figure out the rules before anything fun happens they bail, so try dropping them straight into a super easy level that teaches by doing and save the clever stuff for level 3+

replies.author: TommyGameDev
replies.body:
Yea, I hear you, and that’s also what I tried to do, but I both see people spending 3 minutes on level 5 and others skipping ahead because it’s too easy.

I don’t know how to strike the correct balance. Maybe having better hints or help could be a way

comments.author: Grand_Harbor2440
comments.body: I've seen this with puzzle games that rely on visual polish, players get drawn in by the look but don't stick because the core loop lacks progression or feedback. did you add any subtle rewards for solving puzzles, like a small animation or sound that builds momentum?

replies.author: TommyGameDev
replies.body:
I’m still working on improving the sound design, which I struggle with getting Claude to build for me, but I should also try some more celebratory or momentum-based animation. 

Great input, thank you, I’ll give it some thought!

replies.author: TrollInAnBadMood
replies.body: Sound design is something AI is weak at, that requires a human ear.

comments.author: I_Study_The_Patterns
comments.body: It’s like one of those puzzles in Spider-Man, it’s fine in a short dose but it gets old fast as I don’t think the concept can hold its own for an entire game

comments.author: toothpastespiders
comments.body: 99% of the time I see something interesting and try it out I'm doing so during a quick break or waiting for something. 5 minutes or so is my average first impression time for just about everything. Doesn't mean I'm not going to come back to it later in a weekend or two.

comments.author: Wangcai2976
comments.body: I played it and it's good, the kind of game I'd play when I'm on my computer with nothing else to do. The puzzle mechanics are interesting, and it works well as a time-killer. However, there are already tons of time-killing puzzle games out there with strong progression/reward systems. Maybe think more about who your target audience is, and when and where they would actually play this.

comments.author: Brettinabox
comments.body: "I struggle to get players to stay for longer than 5 minutes." i liked it. very shallow. theres no progression.
